S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any death, serious injury, fire, thermal runaway, or other thermal event presenting a material risk to the regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a written incident report within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a material risk to their unit or requires immediate customer action; other material safety notices must be sent promptly and no later than 10 business days after confirmation.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Exceeding the benchmark alone shall not automatically prohibit sale: the regulator shall set a reasonable, risk-based compliance period and interim safeguards, considering test results and incident data, before deciding on restrictions. Results need not be published publicly by individual company or model, but customers considering or owning a specific model must receive that model's test results, including its failure rate.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Newly installed home battery systems must support remote emergency shut-off. For units already installed that lack this capability, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent compliant upgrade within six years of this standard's effective date.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard's adoption. This requirement does not replace other applicable fire-safety protections.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period; the manufacturer shall promptly notify regulators and affected customers and implement the regulator-approved recall and remedy.

document.section_notes: S2 is the most consequential weakening: exceeding 5% triggers only regulator-set compliance periods with no automatic sales stop, which protects Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%), while customers still receive numeric per-model failure rates and nothing is public. S5 keeps the 8-per-100k mandatory recall with no interim window, which bites on Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9), and S3's six-year retrofit (within the acceptable range) and S4's 36-month suppression deadline (at the edge of the acceptable range) reflect the two companies' respective cost and installed-base positions. Scope in S1 is limited to material-risk thermal events, which I coded as serious_only, although the 24-hour reporting window is tight; the 'other' deadline is set to the same 24-hour rule because the text places all material-risk thermal events under it.
